info.title: OpenRails
info.description: OpenRails' HTTP API, from the API root: a standalone server serves it at /, an embedded host beneath its mount (usually /billing). Generated from the route catalog (internal/http/routes) by `go run ./scripts/contracts -write`; do not edit.

get.description: GetPublicConfig reads the deployment's capabilities and public configuration. It sends no credential and does not invoke the handle's token provider. Over HTTP it is what a browser reads from the same server, ready for a host's page response (billing-ui's BillingProvider config); in process, Engine.PublicConfig names the mount the browser reads.

post.description: CreateInvoice creates a merchant invoice: an unpaid invoice for one customer, which they pay on your site (POST /v1/me/invoices/{id}/pay, or billing-ui's InvoicePayURL). It never charges a card. An invoice in one of the merchant's own units is paid from the customer's balance in it as it is created (insufficient_credits when the balance does not cover it). idempotencyKey is required: a retry with it answers the same invoice.

post.description: ApplyCatalog applies a catalog document as the apply manager. Each product, price key and meter in it applies whole, unless a field it names was set differently by an edit: that object is skipped and listed in the receipt's Conflicts, the rest applies, and the document is not recorded as applied, so applying it again retries the skipped objects. params.Force overwrites those fields instead. The receipt lists deleted objects in Changes with Deleted true, empty Fields and their last Revision before deletion. A document that applied whole and changed the catalog or its ownership is remembered by its canonical content hash: applying it again returns the original receipt even after later catalog edits. It is an operator action, never a side effect of starting: run it from a command (openrails catalog apply, or the host's own) or the console.

post.description: CheckEntitlements is the programmatic content gate: which of params.Entitlements params.CustomerID holds, and the keys they hold under each of params.Prefixes, at params.At (zero: now); every requested key and prefix is in the answer. One call checks at most billing.MaxEntitlementChecks keys and billing.MaxEntitlementPrefixes prefixes; more is refused with invalid_param, not split. It needs an application holding billing.MerchantEntitlementsRead or RootEntitlementsRead (RouteGroups.Programmatic). A remote client answers a current exact-key check from its entitlement cache when every key is allowed there (EntitlementCheckCacheOptions), unless the handle is Uncached; a denial always asks OpenRails.

post.description: CreateProductAccess grants 1 to billing.MaxBatchItems products free, across any customers, all or none; the answer is in request order. Each grant is a window of its product: the customer holds the product's current keys while it is live. idempotencyKey is required: a retry with it replays the first answer and grants nothing again; a retry with other items or terms is idempotency_key_reused. A retry after staff removed a window it granted (revoked before it started) is resource_conflict; grant again under a new key.

post.description: SyncLeases syncs one lease, the protocol under Gate (hosts call NewGate). A sync carries the lease's usage, numbered within the lease, what its gate has had in flight across a sync and the customers whose views it asks for; it settles all the usage it carries and answers how far the usage settled (a resend is matched by lease and number), each view (where the customer stands on its limits, reserving nothing), the limit set of each invoker's attributes, the pricing a gate costs requests with, and how many of the merchant's leases are live. The first sync under a new LeaseID creates the lease; a lease answers resends for 61 days after its last sync. Settled usage posts to the ledger daily, once its day ends in the merchant's accounting zone, and before any other movement of the customer's balance.

post.description: RefundPayment refunds a charge through its rail. The returned refund has Status "succeeded" once the provider confirmed it, or "pending" while the durable refund operation is parked (provider write gates) or reconciling an uncertain provider outcome; it settles without another call. A provider refusal is a StatusError and leaves no refund recorded. idempotencyKey is required: a retry with it returns the same refund and never refunds twice; the same key with other terms is ErrIdempotencyKeyReused.

get.description:
ExportBillingArchive writes the bound merchant's versioned billing archive. Stop source writers for the final cutover export. Authentication identities, provider credentials and live jobs are not portable billing records.

The writer may contain incomplete bytes when an error is returned; publish a file only after success. The Client verifies the archive's integrity footer, and uses the same credential, merchant binding and timeout as other methods.

post.description: ApplyPSPImport lands the import's linked records as customers, payment methods, subscriptions and payments, then approves its corrections (the proposals that keep or extend access) in the caller's name. Only a person signed in, or the in-process host, applies; one holding merchant:customer:manage too approves the corrections that move a subscription's price or terms, and without it an import with one open is refused. It runs in the background. A subscription lands on the provider price mapping its plan; one whose plan is unmapped stays blocked until it is mapped (CreateProviderPrice), linked and applied again.

Error.description: code is stable and listed in x-openrails-error-codes; type and status follow from it; message is diagnostic and not contract.

invoice.description: The invoice a failed payment left open (402 card_error).

Error.description: A refusal: a code of the operation's x-openrails-errors or of an x-openrails-error-sets set it names.

bearer.description: An API key, a service or delegated token, or a user session token.

alert_email_required.meaning: The merchant has no alert_email to send a test message to.

already_owned.meaning: The customer already holds what a line buys; metadata.owned_by names the holder and metadata.hint says change or resume.

application_required.meaning: The route is your backend's: it takes an application's credential, never a person's.

as_of_required.meaning: The import needs as_of, its RFC 3339 evidence horizon.

authentication_unavailable.meaning: The credential could not be verified right now; retry.

authorization_unavailable.meaning: Permissions could not be checked right now; retry.

billing_archive_integrity.meaning: The billing archive failed integrity validation.

billing_archive_invalid_artifact.meaning: The billing archive is invalid, incomplete or unsupported.

billing_archive_merchant_mismatch.meaning: The archive's merchant is not the destination's.

billing_archive_not_empty.meaning: The destination's billing state must be empty.

billing_archive_platform_cards.meaning: The merchant holds cards in the platform vault; export or remove them first.

billing_archive_unsupported_state.meaning: The merchant has state that cannot safely be moved.

billing_details_required.meaning: A billing detail the merchant's checkout.billing_fields require of a new card is missing; param names it.

billing_policy_not_found.meaning: The billing policy does not exist.

cancel_unsupported_on_rail.meaning: This rail has no cancel operation.

captcha_required.meaning: The caller must solve a captcha and resend with its token.

card_attempts_blocked.meaning: Too many declined card attempts; try again later.

card_declined.meaning: The provider declined the card; metadata.decline_reason says why.

card_not_saved.meaning: The card was not saved; enter it again.

card_requires_https.meaning: Card data is accepted only over HTTPS.

card_vault_unknown.meaning: settings.card_vault names no live card PSP of the merchant, nor platform.

catalog_benefit_overlap.meaning: Two recurring products would grant one entitlement outside a shared tier group; put them in one tier group.

catalog_revision_conflict.meaning: The catalog changed during the application; retry.

charge_psp_incompatible.meaning: A charge PSP cannot charge cards from the card vault: a PSP-vaulted card charges only through its own account, a custodian's card through the PSPs naming that custodian.

charge_psp_unknown.meaning: settings.charge_psps names a PSP that is not a live card PSP of the merchant.

credential_revoked.meaning: The credential or its session was revoked.

credit_grant_held.meaning: A refund of the grant's payment is in flight: retry once it settles.

credit_grant_not_found.meaning: The credit grant does not exist.

credit_grant_unavailable.meaning: The credit grant expired, ended or has no remaining credit.

csrf_origin_denied.meaning: A cookie-authenticated request came from an origin that is not allowed.

currency_unsupported.meaning: The currency is not in OpenRails' registry.

custodian_capture_unavailable.meaning: The card custodian cannot capture cards right now.

customer_action_required.meaning: Only the customer may take this action, through their own step.

customer_email_required.meaning: The rail needs the customer's verified email and username.

customer_issuer_mismatch.meaning: The customer belongs to another issuer's user with the same subject.

customer_payment_unsupported.meaning: Customer-present payment is unsupported for this rail or method.

customer_session_required.meaning: The operation needs the customer's interactive session.

customer_tenant_mismatch.meaning: The signed-in account does not belong to this merchant's tenant.

dashboard_invalid.meaning: The dashboard is invalid; metadata.errors lists why.

database_busy.meaning: No database connection is available; retry shortly.

default_payment_method_invalid.meaning: The card cannot be the customer's default for the currency.

default_payment_method_required.meaning: The customer has no default card for the currency.

default_rate_card_not_found.meaning: The meter has no default rate card.

destructive_actions_held.meaning: The merchant's destructive actions are disarmed (`openrails merchant destructive`) or under a destructive hold, so a change that ends access or writes to a provider waits; the proposal stays open.

embed_origins_required.meaning: An embedded pay URL needs the origins that may frame it: the merchant's settings checkout.embed_origins.

entitlement_required.meaning: A line's product sells only to customers who already hold its required entitlements; param names the line and metadata.missing the keys the customer lacks.

event_cursor_expired.meaning: The event cursor is no longer retained; resynchronize current state.

event_store_required.meaning: The deployment has no event store (ClickHouse): usage reporting, meters, limits, usage rate cards, spend windows, failed-usage windows and usage history are off.

finding_action_failed.meaning: Running the finding's recommendation failed; the finding stays open with the error in its notes.

finding_not_actionable.meaning: The finding carries no recommendation to approve; ignore it or fix it out of band.

finding_requires_merchant_config.meaning: The finding is a pull.* proposal: it is approved or dismissed as a proposal, with merchant config.

host_event_not_found.meaning: The host event does not exist.

host_principal_invalid.meaning: The in-process host principal is bound to no merchant, or names an invalid invoker.

idempotency_key_in_use.meaning: The request first sent with this Idempotency-Key is still running; retry once it finishes.

idempotency_key_required.meaning: The operation needs an Idempotency-Key header.

idempotency_key_reused.meaning: The idempotency key already committed with different terms.

insufficient_credits.meaning: The customer's credit balance does not cover the operation.

internal_error.meaning: OpenRails failed; request_id identifies the failure in its logs.

invalid_cursor.meaning: The cursor is not one this list issued.

invalid_customer_id.meaning: The customer id is missing or malformed.

invalid_param.meaning: The request is malformed or a parameter is invalid; param names the parameter when known.

invalid_payment_method.meaning: The payment method is not eligible for this operation.

invalid_query.meaning: A query parameter is malformed or out of range; param is the parameter.

invalid_request_body.meaning: The request body could not be read or is not one JSON value.

invalid_settlement_status_request.meaning: A settlement status read needs a customer and a price.

invoice_action_not_allowed.meaning: The invoice's origin or status does not allow this action.

invoice_attempt_closed.meaning: The invoice attempt already completed or was canceled.

invoice_attempt_expired.meaning: The invoice attempt expired before it was paid.

invoice_has_recurring_line.meaning: An invoice with a recurring line is paid by the customer, whose card its renewals charge; it cannot be recorded as paid.

invoice_line_unavailable.meaning: A line cannot be bought; param names it and metadata.code says why.

invoice_not_cancelable.meaning: Only an open invoice, or one awaiting the customer's action, can be canceled.

invoice_not_payable.meaning: The invoice takes no payment: it is paid, canceled or expired.

invoice_payment_in_progress.meaning: A payment on this invoice is unresolved; read the invoice.

invoice_total_changed.meaning: The invoice's total is not expected_total; preview it again.

invoker_scoped_principal.meaning: An invoker-scoped credential spends a customer's balance but may not manage the account.

lease_not_found.meaning: No lease of the merchant has this id, which is older than the replay horizon; start a new lease.

limit_not_found.meaning: The catalog declares no limit under this key.

merchant_config_read_only.meaning: The merchant's configuration is read from a file; change the file.

merchant_mismatch.meaning: The credential is bound to a different merchant than OpenRails-Expected-Merchant; the operation was not executed.

merchant_unit_unsupported.meaning: The currency is one of the merchant's own units, which the operation does not take: it takes a currency from OpenRails' registry.

merchant_unresolved.meaning: The credential is bound to no merchant here.

message_send_failed.meaning: The email sender did not accept the message.

message_template_invalid.meaning: The message template does not render against its event type's sample data; the message says why.

meter_in_use.meaning: The meter is referenced and cannot change this way.

meter_rate_card_conflict.meaning: The meter and its rate card disagree.

method_not_allowed.meaning: The path exists but not for this method; Allow lists its methods.

metrics_query_invalid.meaning: The metrics query is invalid; metadata.errors lists why.

pay_url_attempts_exhausted.meaning: The pay URL took its most card attempts; the merchant creates a new invoice.

pay_url_expired.meaning: The pay URL expired; the merchant creates a new invoice.

pay_url_not_found.meaning: The pay URL is unknown or no longer valid.

pay_url_unavailable.meaning: This deployment serves no checkout origin, or the invoice cannot take a pay URL.

payment_duplicate_refused.meaning: The provider refused an identical charge it had just made; retry after its duplicate window.

payment_exceeds_due.meaning: A recorded payment must equal the invoice's total; a usage payment must not exceed the amount due.

payment_idempotency_conflict.meaning: The idempotency key belongs to another payment request.

payment_in_progress.meaning: A payment is already unresolved; read the resource before retrying.

payment_method_delete_failed.meaning: The provider could not delete the payment method.

payment_method_delete_unsupported.meaning: This payment method cannot be deleted through OpenRails.

payment_method_not_psp_vaulted.meaning: The payment method is not held in the provider vault.

payment_method_not_usable.meaning: The payment method cannot be charged in its current state.

payment_method_psp_mismatch.meaning: The payment method is vaulted by another PSP than the subscription's.

payment_method_required.meaning: The charge names neither a saved payment method nor a new card token.

payment_method_same_vault.meaning: The card is in the provider vault the subscription already bills.

payment_method_stale.meaning: The saved payment method can no longer be charged; collect the card again.

payment_method_update_failed.meaning: The provider could not update the payment method.

payment_method_update_unsupported.meaning: This payment method cannot be updated through OpenRails.

payment_not_refundable.meaning: The payment is not a completed rail charge, or the amount exceeds what remains refundable.

payment_not_retryable.meaning: The resource is not payable now.

payment_option_unavailable.meaning: No PSP that can take the invoice's lines accepts this payment.

payment_provider_rejected.meaning: The provider refused to process the charge for a gateway or account reason.

permission_required.meaning: The credential lacks the permission the route requires.

person_required.meaning: Only a person signed in, or the embedding host in process, may take this action; an API key or service token may not.

platform_vault_mixed_class.meaning: The platform vault's charge PSPs mix live and test; one platform identity holds one money class.

platform_vault_unavailable.meaning: The deployment has no platform vault for its posture, or its identity for this merchant names another vault tenant; save cards at a PSP's vault.

platform_vault_unreachable.meaning: A charge PSP cannot charge cards from the platform vault (Stripe, or card_entry server); leave it out of charge_psps or save cards at a PSP's vault.

price_change_currency_mismatch.meaning: The target price must be in the subscription's currency.

price_increase_notice_too_short.meaning: effective_at is inside the merchant's notice window for a price increase.

price_key_cadence_conflict.meaning: The product's default price key is held by a price on another cadence.

price_migration_in_progress.meaning: The same price migration is being created by another request; retry once it answers.

price_migration_not_found.meaning: The price migration does not exist.

price_not_sellable.meaning: None of the price's methods can sell it.

product_in_use.meaning: Records refer to the product; archive it instead.

product_tier_group_conflict.meaning: A customer holds live subscriptions to more than one product of the tier group.

product_tier_group_in_use.meaning: The tier group cannot change while a subscription has a plan change in flight.

provider_cancel_held.meaning: Canceling needs a destructive provider action that is not armed for this merchant.

provider_outcome_unknown.meaning: The provider did not confirm the outcome; read the resource before retrying.

provider_price_unreadable.meaning: The provider did not answer for the provider price's terms; retry.

provider_writes_disabled.meaning: Provider writes are off for the merchant, so it takes no payment; the message names why (the merchant's write posture).

provider_writes_held.meaning: The merchant's writes are `readonly` (`openrails merchant writes`), so a change that moves money or writes to a provider waits; the proposal stays open.

psp_claim_requires_proof.meaning: Claiming a provider account needs credentials that prove control of it.

psp_credentials_rejected.meaning: The provider rejected the credentials, or answered that they are not in the PSP's declared environment.

psp_environment_refused.meaning: A live PSP is refused where the deployment wires fake providers.

psp_exists.meaning: The account is already a PSP, of this merchant or another; update it instead.

psp_import_in_progress.meaning: Another import of the PSP is pulling or applying; wait for it to finish.

psp_key_taken.meaning: Another live PSP holds the key.

psp_last_active.meaning: The PSP is the last active one on its rail; pass allow_last to archive it.

psp_probe_limited.meaning: The provider refused this login twice within the hour, or it is being checked, and it locks out repeated failed logins; Retry-After says when it may be checked again.

purchase_review_resolved.meaning: The purchase review was already resolved.

quantity_not_allowed.meaning: A quantity was sent for a price that is not sold per seat.

rate_card_product_not_found.meaning: The rate card names a product that does not exist.

rate_limit_exceeded.meaning: Too many requests; Retry-After says when to try again.

rebill_terms_committed.meaning: An accepted recurring payment owns the pending price terms.

refund_rail_unavailable.meaning: The payment's rail cannot accept a refund right now.

refund_unsupported.meaning: The payment's rail has no automatic refund.

request_body_too_large.meaning: The request body exceeds the deployment's cap.

resource_access_denied.meaning: The credential may not access this resource.

resource_conflict.meaning: The request conflicts with the resource's current state.

resource_not_found.meaning: The addressed resource does not exist in this merchant.

revision_mismatch.meaning: The object changed since the revision the edit expected; metadata.revision is the current one.

running_charge_not_found.meaning: No running charge was started under this reference.

scheduled_change_exists.meaning: The subscription already has a scheduled change.

service_credential_customer_scope_denied.meaning: The service credential may not act for this customer.

service_unavailable.meaning: A dependency is temporarily unavailable; retry.

solana_rpc_unavailable.meaning: The Solana RPC endpoints did not answer; retry.

solana_transaction_refused.meaning: The wallet transaction could not be prepared or confirmed; the message says why.

step_up_required.meaning: The operation needs a recent sign-in (RFC 9470: WWW-Authenticate insufficient_user_authentication with max_age); metadata carries the provider's challenge.

step_up_unavailable.meaning: The operation needs a recent sign-in and this credential cannot prove one.

stored_credential_required.meaning: The card has no active agreement for a merchant-initiated charge; the customer makes this change.

subscription_change_already_scheduled.meaning: A different period-end change is already scheduled.

subscription_change_cadence_unsupported.meaning: A provider-billed subscription can change only to a price of the same cadence.

subscription_change_credit_exceeds_price.meaning: The current plan's unused value exceeds the target price; change at period end.

subscription_change_cycle_unknown.meaning: The target price has no positive billing cycle.

subscription_change_idempotency_conflict.meaning: The Idempotency-Key already names a different change.

subscription_change_idempotency_key_requ.meaning: A subscription change needs an Idempotency-Key.

subscription_change_in_flight.meaning: Another unresolved change owns the subscription: read it back with its Idempotency-Key, or confirm it.

subscription_change_period_unknown.meaning: The subscription has no valid current period.

subscription_change_provider_conflict.meaning: The provider's copy of the subscription is missing or differs; reconcile it first.

subscription_change_refused.meaning: The change was refused and not executed.

subscription_change_renewal_due.meaning: The current period ended or its renewal is unresolved; the renewal settles first.

subscription_change_requires_linked_plan.meaning: The target price has no plan on the subscription's PSP that this change can use.

subscription_change_target_inactive.meaning: The target price or its product is archived.

subscription_change_unsupported_on_rail.meaning: The subscription's rail cannot make this change.

subscription_paid_through.meaning: A canceled subscription to this product is still paid; buy again once its paid period ends.

subscription_resumable.meaning: A canceled subscription to this product is still paid and can be resumed; resume it instead of buying again.

too_many_buckets.meaning: The window at the interval holds more buckets than a series answers (a usage series: 1,000); shorten the window or widen the interval. param is interval.

trial_unsupported_on_rail.meaning: This rail cannot run a trial first phase.

unknown_field.meaning: The JSON body names a field the route does not accept; param is the field.

unsupported_media_type.meaning: The request body is not application/json.

usage_events_expired.meaning: Usage by invoker reads raw usage events, kept 90 days; the window starts before them. History by event type and meter reaches back further. param is the window's start.

usage_meter_not_found.meaning: The usage meter does not exist.

usage_not_priced.meaning: A priced meter cannot price the usage (no matrix cell for its value, or no rate card in its currency); param names the field.

usage_out_of_order.meaning: A usage item skips a number the lease has not settled; send the items in order.

usage_rate_card_invalid.meaning: The usage rate card is invalid.

webhook_account_mismatch.meaning: The webhook's account does not match its payload.
